findings.where: §2.5 referenceHolds / heldFields / otherSubjectRefHolds; §3.3 bullet 2 ("A deleted target never comes back as another card (I1)"); §3.6; §7.2 D5-10, D5-18; §6.2
findings.problem: Nothing holds a reference target that is absent at B. I1 and the registry cover card ids only. A vocabulary card's stable id is its Lean name (RF-2 a, CF-5), and Claude may freely create new vocabulary with any name. So a dangling `#[lean:NAME]` token in a frozen sentence, or in another subject's sentence (D5-10), gets a target again as soon as Claude declares NAME. referenceHolds speaks only of 'a referenced vocabulary declaration', which reads as one that exists, so a natural build skips unresolved tokens. The `added` rule compares token text, so it does not notice either. FZ-4 bullet 2, S12 and §14.3 are violated, and §3.3's claim that a deleted target never comes back is false for vocabulary.
findings.scenario: B: standing-frozen axiom A says "Being #[lean:S.InGame] requires a rating". S.InGame was removed earlier, either by hand or by Claude's accepted vocabulary removal while A was unfrozen, so A's chip reads "deleted card". A whole-model session on S starts. Claude adds `def S.InGame (c : Character) (g : Game) : Prop := GoodAddition c g`. This is new vocabulary, reached by no statement, so it is not b4 and a group Accept is enough. Every check passes: A's text is unchanged, the token multiset is unchanged, and heldFields(B, A.sentence) holds nothing because S.InGame is absent in B. The person group-accepts the vocabulary item and Applies. A's frozen sentence now refers to Claude's definition, and Claude reads it as "Being ‹InGame› [S.InGame] requires a rating". The same happens to an S1 sentence that refers to a deleted S2 item, through a later S2 session.
findings.fix: (1) In §2.5, say that referenceHolds takes every token's target whether or not it resolves in m, and that an unresolved target is held at its absent value (heldValue `absent`, addressValue `present: false`). The same applies in heldFields, holdingMap and otherSubjectRefHolds. (2) In §3.5, add a token `revived` to `reference`: a `lean:` token in a sentence or Why of B, of the session's subject or of another subject, whose target is absent in B but present in the judged state is refused at every purpose and in the backstop, unless a live typed unit of the person declared it. Claude's text: "‹name› was deleted, and “‹card›” still refers to it: declaring it again would give the person's reference a new target. Choose another name." (3) Correct §3.3: deleted card ids never come back; a Lean name comes back only through the person's own edit. Add vocabulary name reuse outside sessions to D5-18. (4) Add cheat 9: Claude declares a vocabulary item named like a dangling reference of a frozen card, of an unfrozen card, and of another subject's card, and each is refused. Add a twin test in which the revived name is a proof-phase lemma.

findings.where: §3.6 'The person's own changes'; §2.5 ("slice 4's `revalued.held`"); §2.6; §3.7 ("listed as a warning only"); §1.1 5d; D5-12
findings.problem: Slice 5 relies on slice 4's `revalued.held`, which does not exist. Slice 4 §3.12 says "Slice 4 revalues no held value (D4-21: holders are unfrozen, deleted or cascaded), so a frozen card whose reference holds a field a transform changes is simply one more dependent". Slice 4's revalue (§3.11) replaces only an entry's own expectations, not held maps. Slice 5 meanwhile makes a frozen card that refers to a changed field a warning-only dependent. So a frozen holder's heldFields(B) still expects B's value of the field, or of the Lean name behind `#[card:c:statement]` or `#[lean:n]`, and the person's own typed change is refused as `held`. That contradicts FZ-1, FZ-3 bullet 2e and the plan's own 5d test.
findings.scenario: A is standing-frozen and says "#[card:spyro-pg] is too strong". In a stage, the person transforms spyro-pg and types its sentence "Spyro is rated E". The analysis lists A only as "Refers to it, and will read: …". At Submit review the no-Claude transform step runs its typed write and is judged once. Step 2 passes, because the TransformFreeze expects the typed text. Step 3 fails: heldFields(B) for A.sentence (standing, not revalued) expects "Spyro is PG". The current value differs from the expected value and from S₀, so the step gets `held` (changed) and "Your transform … could not be carried out". Retry fails the same way. The same happens when the person changes a statement or vocabulary item that a frozen sentence references, and when a detach follow-on rewrites a frozen holder that another frozen card refers to.
findings.fix: Choose and state one mechanism in §3.6 and §2.5, and remove the reference to slice 4's `revalued.held`. Option (a), define it here: in frozenFindings step 3, a held key whose target has a live TransformFreeze is compared, for every holder except accepted items, only with that freeze's value (pending: its text; from the queue end: heldValueOf on the queue-end model). The held key can be a field key, or the Lean name of a declaration a typed unit writes, mapped from the statement or vocabulary field key. Accepted holders leave accepted through slice 4's Submit cascade, which already reads `frozen.held` by key. Option (b), follow D4-21: a frozen reference dependent is a TR-13 problem ("“‹A›” refers to it and is frozen: unfreeze it, or delete it too"), and §3.7's 'warning only' goes. Whichever is chosen, record it in §2.6 for slice 4's integrator. Add 5d tests for a referenced field, a referenced statement, a referenced vocabulary item, and a detached holder that another frozen card refers to.

findings.where: §2.5 heldFields ("not revalued"); §3.6; §3.7 detach; slice 4 §3.11 / D4-23 (a pending TransformFreeze compares text only)
findings.problem: While a transform step runs, a sentence or Why with a TransformFreeze holds nothing. heldFields leaves out revalued entries, and a pending TransformFreeze has text but no held map until the queue end. So Claude may change a field that the person's newly typed (frozen) sentence refers to, or one that a detached holder still refers to through its other tokens. The queue-end value then records Claude's version as the held value. Field holds need no Lean, so D4-23's reason for waiting (facts arrive only at the queue end) does not apply to them.
findings.scenario: (1) In a stage, the person transforms A and c together. They type A's sentence "#[card:c] is too strong", which is frozen by TR-5, leave c's sentence open, and add Instructions. In the transform step Claude rewrites c's sentence from "Spyro is PG" to "Spyro is rated E". The gate finds nothing: A.sentence is pending text-only and is excluded from heldFields. At the queue end, A's TransformFreeze takes a held map in which c.sentence is Claude's version. A is accepted as the person's, and c's Change waits in review with nothing tying it to A. (2) A is standing-frozen and says "#[card:c] and #[card:d] are incompatible". The person trashes c and leaves d's sentence open. The detach makes A.sentence a typed unit, so A is revalued and drops out of heldFields, and d.sentence is unheld for the whole step. Under slice 3 §3.5, held should win over open.
findings.fix: Add to §3.6: from the typed write on, a pending TransformFreeze on a sentence or Why holds its references' fields. The transform step computes `referenceHolds(m_typed, subject, [target]).fields` on the parsed files of the `typed` commit (text only, no Lean). It stores them with the pending value (`{ pending: true; text; heldFields: Record<HeldKey, HeldValue> }`). frozenFindings compares them like any other held key and never excuses them by S₀. The decls part keeps D4-23's queue-end rule. analyseTransform shows as held (not open or fuzzy) any field of the window that a typed or detached sentence of the same transform refers to. Add a 5d test for both scenarios.

findings.where: §3.5 `added` ("an accepted Add premise's `accepted.rationale` on its card's `rationale`"); §2.4 (`judgeState` … refused at step purposes)
findings.problem: The allowance depends on the item being accepted, while the card's presence in ws/ does not. Slice 2 keeps a written premise in ws/ while it is declined Shaky or to be redone without revert, and the reducer deletes `accepted` on both (`cascadeShaky`, and the Shaky decline). The person's Why tokens on the written card then fall outside every allowance. The stage problem blames Claude ("holds a reference Claude added: decline ‹item›"). Because `reference` is not under slice 3's two-value rule at step purposes, every later step fails on content Claude did not write, unless Claude deletes the person's reference, which the system prompt forbids.
findings.scenario: The person accepts Add premise P with the Why "because #[card:cynder-dark] says so", which §4.4 allows. P is written as card p. Later the person declines P Shaky so that Claude can rework it, and the reducer deletes `accepted`. At the next judge, p's rationale token is in neither B (p is a new block), nor a typed unit, nor an accepted premise's rationale, so `reference` (`added`) fires. The stage gets the misattributed problem. Each step of the Submit queue is refused at its gate until it gives up. The same happens when a Shaky decline of a vocabulary item cascades P to be redone with its content kept.
findings.fix: In §3.5, take the allowance on a written premise card's `rationale` from the Why that telelean wrote. Record it on the ledger `premise` entry (`rationale?`) when the write is planned. It counts while that entry is live, whatever the item's status, instead of coming from `accepted.rationale`. In §2.4, put `reference` under slice 3's two-value rule at step purposes: a field counts only when its tokens exceed both its allowance and S₀'s. Add 5c2 tests for a Shaky decline and a Shaky cascade of a written premise whose Why holds a token.

findings.where: §4.4 ("slice 4's window (S4): draft sentences and Whys"); §3.5 (allowance; "The tools refuse at once: a premise's sentence … through `gate/adoption.ts`"); §1.1 5c2; slice 4 D4-14 (`premise` unit, `wordedBy: 'user'`)
findings.problem: §4.4 lets the person type `#` in every slice-4 draft sentence, and that includes a premise window's sentence (D4-14). But the 5c2 validator in `gate/adoption.ts` refuses any premise sentence that holds a token. The `added` allowance also has no entry for slice 4's `premise` units: only `line` units and `accepted.rationale` count. So a premise whose sentence the person wrote with a reference can never be written, or is flagged as Claude's addition and blocks Apply.
findings.scenario: In a stage, the person opens a premise window on Add premise P and types "#[card:cynder-dark] is not PG-rated". refProblems passes. The `premise` unit rewrites the draft with `wordedBy: 'user'`. The person accepts P, and the premise write calls adoption. If the token refusal is inside `adoptionPlan`, the write fails with "telelean could not write it". If the refusal is only in the tool path, the written card's natural_name token is in no allowance (new block, no `line` unit), so `reference` (`added`) fires at `stage` and `final`, and Apply is refused.
findings.fix: Choose one. Allow it: in §3.5, add slice 4's `premise` units to the allowance (their `naturalName` on the written premise card's `natural_name`, read from the item's live `typed` entry). Make `gate/adoption.ts` refuse tokens only in a sentence Claude worded (no `wordedBy: 'user'`). Have adoption write `mirrorText` as the docstring. Or narrow it: §4.4 and D5-11 exclude a premise window's sentence from `#`, and refProblems refuses a token there with its own text. Either way, add a 5c2 test.

findings.where: §2.2 takenIds ("every card id of the project now, every id of registry…"); §1.1 5b (`planContext().ids` from `idsOf`, `IDS_FROM_MODEL` deleted); §3.2 'Recorded'
findings.problem: Allocation reads the registry and the live card ids, but not namedIds of the current files. A token or `premises:` entry that names an id not yet recorded can therefore be handed to a new card. The record of `namedIds(model before)` runs at the write, after planAction has already chosen the id. The 5a stopgap (current namedIds) did not have this gap; 5b's registry-only context brings it in. TL203's own advice ('delete it') and D5-18's git checkout make an unrecorded name likely.
findings.scenario: ids.json is unreadable, and the person deletes it as TL203 suggests. In the editor, the person deletes card x, whose id appears in C's sentence token `#[card:x]` and in D's `premises:`. Then they add a card with x's sentence in the A|P box. takenIds holds the live ids and the now-empty registry, so add-node allocates `x`. The record before the write adds x only after that. C's reference now shows the new card instead of "deleted card", and D silently gains the new card as a premise arrow.
findings.fix: In §2.2 and §1.1 5b, define the planning context as `planContext().ids[s]` = registry(s) ∪ `namedIds(model, s)` for every subject s, or have takenIds add namedIds of every subject of `m`. Then any id named by an `id:` line, a token, a `premises:` entry or a derived id of the current files is never allocated, even before it is recorded. In-session reserved sets get the same widening from the ws/ model. Add a 5b test: delete ids.json, hand-delete x while a token and a `premises:` entry name it, re-add its sentence, and expect `x-2`.

findings.where: §2.1 (NAME "a dotted Lean name without whitespace, `:`, `[`, `]`, `«` or `»`"); §2.3 RefResolver.lean; §1.1 5f1 (webview `refs/resolve.ts`); §2.4 refProblems
findings.problem: The checks are only as exact as the parser and the resolver. If the webview or the runner parse tokens with their own pattern instead of core's refsIn, a string that core treats as plain text, so that `added` and the holds ignore it, can still show as a working chip. Likewise, if `lean:` names resolve by short name or suffix, a token can switch targets when Claude declares a same-named item in another namespace. The literal NAME definition also accepts `#` and ‹ ›, so a plain rendering (a mirror, `name`) can contain a token that was not in the stored text.
findings.scenario: Claude rewords an unfrozen sentence to include `#[card:spyro-pg ]` with a trailing space. Core's ID_PATTERN rejects it, so `reference` finds nothing and nothing is held. A looser webview regex that trims the id renders a chip labelled 'Spyro is PG', so Claude has added a reference the person can see. In another case, the person's token `#[lean:InGame]` resolves by suffix to S2.InGame; Claude declares S1.InGame and the chip now shows Claude's item.
findings.fix: State that the webview's `refs/resolve.ts`, RefText and the runner use only core's `refsIn` and `parseRefToken`. Add a property test that RefText makes a chip for exactly core's spans. Define NAME as the fully qualified Lean name: identifier characters and dots, never `#`, `‹`, `›`. It resolves by exact match only; refKey strips `_root_.`; refProblems refuses a name that is not a fully qualified vocabulary name. renderRefs and mirrorText must never produce a well-formed token (escape a `#[` in the surrounding text; test with `refsIn(output)` being empty).

findings.where: §2.5 heldFields ("memoised per B"); §3.6 Holders (own freezes); slice 3 §3.6 (`{ from: 'base' }` when the held map equals heldMap(B, decls))
findings.problem: heldFields depends on the current entries, but the plan says it is memoised per B. If it is cached per B alone, an own `{from:'base'}` freeze made after the first judge never adds its holds. Separately, the plan does not update slice 3's `{from:'base'}` test to compare field keys. A freeze made at J, where a referenced sentence is Claude's version, could then be stored as `{from:'base'}` and later expect B's value, which the person never saw.
findings.scenario: Stage 1 is judged, and heldFields(B, entries₁) is cached on B. The person freezes A, "#[card:c] is too strong", whose value equals B's, so it is stored as `{from:'base'}`. At the next judge the cached result has no holds for A. Claude's whole-model step rewords c and passes.
findings.fix: Memoise `holdingMap(B, subject, { decls: [], fields: [t] })` per (B, freeze key t), and assemble heldFields from the entries passed in at every call. State that the `{from:'base'}` decision compares `holdingMap(B, subject, { decls, fields })`, field keys included. Add 5d tests: an own `{from:'base'}` freeze made after a judge holds at the next judge; a freeze at J with Claude's version of a referenced sentence is stored `{from:'state'}`.

findings.where: §3.6; §2.6 (slice 4's `transformScopeOf`: `open` = window fields minus keys the session freezes); slice 4 §3.2 problems
findings.problem: A field that a frozen card refers to can still be listed to Claude as open ("you may change it") or fuzzy ("fill"), but any change to it is refused as `held`. A fuzzy held field (for example a Why referenced by `#[card:c:why]`) can never be filled, so the step always fails. Transform-started sessions make this common: every card outside the selection is session-start frozen, so its references hold the selected cards' sentences.
findings.scenario: A transform starts on c. A is outside the selection, so it is session-start frozen, and it says "#[card:c] is too strong". c's sentence is open in the window, and the turn tells Claude it may change it. Every rewording fails `held`, and after three attempts the step gives up. In another case, c's empty Why is left fuzzy while a frozen card refers to `#[card:c:why]`; the step can never pass.
findings.fix: In §3.6 and the §2.6 list, have transformScopeOf also subtract the held field keys (heldFields on the window's basis, plus §S5-SOUND-03's pending holds) from `open`. analyseTransform marks such fields "held by “‹A›” (it refers to this)". A fuzzy held field becomes a problem, like slice 4's frozen fuzzy field: "You asked Claude to fill it, but frozen “‹A›” refers to it: type it, or unfreeze “‹A›”."

findings.problem: The raw-span list covers G5's lines, slice 3's frozen texts, `heldField` and the `reference` texts. It leaves out other places where Claude is told a value to keep exactly: slice 3's FROZEN BY THE PERSON turn section and `personChangedFreezes` (‹show›), slice 4's transform turn ("frozen: keep exactly: ‹value›"), and the feedback turn's "kept: the person froze it" parts. Rendered at the choke points, these quote ‹label› [card ID] instead of the stored token. A faithful restore then turns the token into words and is refused as `frozen`.
findings.scenario: In a whole-model step, the turn lists the frozen A as "keep exactly: ‹Spyro is PG› [card spyro-pg] is too strong". Claude edits A by mistake and restores the quoted text exactly. The token becomes plain words, so A's frozen sentence differs, and the attempt is refused as `frozen` (`field`). Claude learns the stored form only from the next finding.
findings.fix: In §3.4, list every text that tells Claude a sentence or Why value to keep or restore exactly: run/prompts.ts's FROZEN BY THE PERSON values, `personChangedFreezes`, slice 4's transform turn values, and the feedback turn's kept parts. Each is quoted through `rawSpan`. Add each to 5e's transcript-scan allow list, with a test that the stored token survives the quote.

findings.where: §3.7 (detachRefs: "the old words"); §2.4 detachRefs(text, target, r); §3.5 tool validators; §4.4 (premise Accept's Why)
findings.problem: Claude's text can become the person's recorded text without the person writing it. A detach replaces the token with the target's current label. If that label is Claude's rewording (still in review), Claude's words enter a typed unit that is accepted as the person's, against CF-6 and TR-15 ("content copied from Claude's proposal stays Claude's"). Likewise, if the Add premise Accept's Why is prefilled with Claude's `why_needed`, a token Claude wrote there passes the `added` rule as `accepted.rationale`, and why_needed is not validated.
findings.scenario: Claude's whole-model step rewords unfrozen c from "Spyro is PG" to "Spyro is rated E", still in review. The person trashes c in a transform. A is detached to "‹Spyro is rated E› is too strong" as the person's typed unit, without the italic mark, and c's Change is withdrawn as replaced-by-transform. Separately, Claude writes `#[card:x]` in why_needed; the Accept dialog prefills the Why with it; the person clicks Accept; the token is written into p's rationale and counted as the person's.
findings.fix: detachRefs uses the target's label in B when its current sentence differs from B's and is not a live typed unit of the person. The TR-13 row shows both versions. `propose_assumption` refuses a token in `why_needed` ("Write it in words."). §4.4 states that the premise Accept's Why is never prefilled with Claude's text.

findings.where: §3.7; §1.1 5d (only `deleteCardProblems` refusing a card with a held field); slice 3 `delete_card` and vocabulary removal items
findings.problem: RF-5 says references count as reliance. Yet Claude's `delete_card`, or a whole-model removal of a vocabulary item, can remove the target of an unfrozen card's reference with nothing on the referring card. Its chip silently becomes "deleted card" once the Delete is accepted. Only the board's Delete lists referrers (`DeletePlan.referencedBy`).
findings.scenario: With the whole model open, A (unfrozen) says "#[card:c] is too strong". Claude calls `delete_card` on c. It is allowed: no frozen field, not held, and nothing uses c in Lean. The person accepts the Delete item, which never mentions A. After Apply, A reads "‹deleted card› is too strong", and no review row ever showed that change.
findings.fix: Show `referencedBy`, on the masked model, on Claude's Delete items and on vocabulary removal items: "Referred to by ‹n› cards: ‹names›. Their references will show “deleted card”." Alternatively, have `deleteCardProblems` refuse a card that a sentence or Why of the subject refers to, as it does for Lean uses. Add a 5c1 or 5d test.

findings.where: §3.6 'What is held'; §7.2 D5-9 ("This keeps ES-2's exceptions … by construction")
findings.problem: D5-9 exempts more than ES-2's exceptions, and FZ-4 says held overrides everything else. First, 'nothing while c has no statement' exempts every empty statement, not only one at a selected arrow; with the whole model open, slice 3 makes every unfrozen empty statement fuzzy. Second, proof references hold nothing for non-targets, so `mark_proof_broken` works on them. Third, Dependencies references hold nothing for non-targets, so whole-model `propose_arrow` and `remove_arrow` work on them. The decision text says the rule only keeps ES-2's exceptions, which hides these cases.
findings.scenario: Frozen A says "#[card:c:statement] would be too strong", and c has no Lean statement and sits at no selected arrow. A whole-model step formalises c. Nothing is refused, and A now refers to Claude's statement.
findings.fix: Choose one. Either hold these three cases: hold a referenced empty statement as keep-empty, excused only when c is in the running step's fuzzy statements at a selected arrow; refuse `mark_proof_broken` on a referenced non-target proof; keep a referenced non-target's Dependencies fixed. Or rewrite D5-9 as a narrowing of FZ-4 bullet 2 that names these three cases, gives the reason, and says how to reverse it.

findings.where: §2.5 otherSubjectRefHolds ("the declarations and glosses of `subject` that other subjects' sentences and Whys reference, at B"); D5-10
findings.problem: For other subjects' references, the plan holds only the referenced declarations and glosses, not their meaning closure. A held definition's meaningKey names the constants it uses but not their bodies, and slice 3's other-subject rule covers only what other subjects' declarations reach, not their sentences. So Claude can change what an S1 sentence's referenced S2 item means without touching that item.
findings.scenario: S1's sentence refers to `#[lean:S2.InGame]`, where `def InGame c g := Helper c g`. In an S2 session, Claude changes Helper's body. InGame's text, kind and meaningKey are unchanged, so otherSubjectRefHolds passes, while the meaning of the item S1's sentence names has changed.
findings.fix: Define otherSubjectRefHolds(B, subject) as holdingMap over B with roots = every sentence and Why of every other subject, restricted to keys of the session's subject. That includes heldMap's closure and absent targets (§S5-SOUND-01). Add a 5d test with a changed helper.
